key_insight: The paper turns quantum teleportation into an interactive communication mechanism for musical agents, using quantum states to mediate improvisational behavior between performers and AI agents.
engineering_relevance: It demonstrates how NISQ-era quantum effects, including noise and decoherence, can be treated as expressive design features in real-time multi-agent systems.
method: Encode melodic and rhythmic behavior as quantum states with SQPAM.
Structure agent dynamics using Quantum Phase Estimation (QPE).
Use directed quantum teleportation to transfer states among up to three agents in one circuit.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analysis using melodic correlation, pitch-set distance, and state fidelity to measure how teleported states balance imitation versus divergence.
watch_item: The approach depends on fragile NISQ hardware behavior, so real-time performance, fidelity, and reproducibility may be limited by noise and circuit complexity.
paper_title: Teleportation Game: Quantum Teleportation in Multi-Agent Systems for Interactive Music
